messages:
Sophie: kicking off a short thread — proposing acceptance checklist for the long-term routing policy DSL migration. TL;DR: we need launch criteria that balance customer asks, rollback safety, and measurable perf/cost impact.
Raj: +1. can we make the acceptance criteria measurable? e.g., p95 latency delta < 10ms, mean cost per 1M tokens delta < 5%?
Ana: those metrics work. also need to include error budget impact and a clear canary plan for retention/eviction scenarios.
Chen: rough rollout: canary 1% (internal), 5% beta (ok customers), 25% gradual; each step gated by automated checks. If failure, immediate fallback to policy v1.
Matt: quick policy snippet we considered:
```
policy v2 {
  match: tenant.region == eu-west
  prefer: low-latency-edge
  fallback: regional-pool
  cost_weight: 0.3
}
```
Kelsey: question — how do we version-control policy changes? need migration tooling + replayable diff + audit logs.
Sophie: agree. launch criteria proposal:
- perf: p95 delta <= 10ms vs baseline
- correctness: routing decisions pass 100% of our unit/test harness for sample tenants
- cost: mean cost delta <= +5% for 30d simulated workload
- ops: canary rollback <5min with automated switch
- security: no cross-tenant routing regressions
Raj: add customer acceptance: two named customers signed off for early beta (Acme, DataCo). Also legal/regulatory for data-residency paths.
infra-bot: automated canary checks: perf-smoke, routing-sanity, evict-sim. Results posted to #eng-oncall.
Chen: operational notes: need runbook for partial-eviction and a "quiet period" before expanding an outlier tenant. Also quota bumping for beta customers.
Ana: next steps: Sophie to write RFC with checklist and sample json-based policy diff format; Chen/infra to prototype automated gating scripts; product to prioritize customer outreach.
Sophie: I'll draft RFC by EOD Friday and tag reviewers. @Kelsey can you own policy audit log schema? :thanks:
Kelsey: on it. will sketch schema + retention options.
Matt: can we include a small simulation harness in the RFC? even simple qps/seq-length mix will help customers sign off.
Sophie: yes — include simulation results for baseline and v2 in RFC. keeping thread short — ping me in here if you have blockers.
